articles.metaTitle: Barber Price List: What to Charge in 2026 | BKRDY
articles.metaDescription: A realistic barber price list for 2026: haircut, fade, beard, and combo pricing, how to set your own numbers, and a clean menu clients can book from.
articles.h1: The barber price list, done right
articles.italicTagline: What to charge, what clients expect, and how to display it so it books.
articles.intro: 180-220 word intro. The SERP for this term is Zazzle posters, Etsy printables, and PosterMyWall templates: everyone is selling a laminated sign, nobody is answering the real question, which is what the numbers on the sign should say. Open with that gap. Promise three things: real 2026 price ranges for the core barber menu (cut, skin fade, beard, kids, combos) split by city tier; a simple method for setting your own prices (costs, time per cut, chair math); and how to present the menu so it converts, because a price list on a website with a Book button outearns a price board on the wall. Natural BKRDY tie: your booking site IS your price list. No em-dashes, confident, no fluff.

sections.title: 2026 barber price ranges, service by service
sections.direction: Table of typical US ranges: haircut, skin fade, beard trim, hot towel shave, kids cut, cut + beard combo. Split budget / mid / premium and note big-city vs small-town spread. Cite ranges honestly as ranges.

sections.title: How to set YOUR prices, not the internet's
sections.direction: Chair math: time per cut, cuts per day, monthly costs, target income. Show one worked example (30-min fades, 10 clients a day). Push back on copying competitor prices without knowing their costs.

sections.title: When and how to raise without losing regulars
sections.direction: Signals you are underpriced (booked out 2+ weeks, no-shows cheap to eat). The announcement script. Grandfathering regulars for one cycle. Link internal: /guides/reducing-no-shows/ and deposit content.

sections.title: A menu clients can actually book from
sections.direction: The wall poster vs the booking page. Every service with price + duration + Book button beats a static list. Screenshot-level description of a BKRDY service menu; CTA to templates and /for-barbers/.

research.serpNotes: Zazzle, Amazon, Etsy, PosterMyWall, Pinterest, one real barbershop page. Printable-template marketplaces, zero SaaS competition, no real article answering what to charge. STRONG opening.

articles.metaTitle: Brow Lamination and Tint: The Combo Explained | BKRDY
articles.metaDescription: Brow lamination and tint in one visit: what the combo does, before and after expectations, how long it lasts, pricing, and how brow techs sell it.
articles.italicTagline: What the combo does, what before and after really looks like, and the tech-side play.
secondaryKeywords: what is brow lamination and tint
how long does brow lamination and tint last
articles.intro: 180-220 word intro. Companion piece to /blog/brow-lamination-cost/ (pending): that one owns the price question, this one owns the what-is and before-and-after questions. SERP is supplier brands (PLA Pro, Supercilium, Lash Lift Store), one franchise blog, and local studios; nobody with real authority. Open on why the combo exists: lamination fixes shape, tint fixes visibility, and tinting AFTER lamination absorbs better because the cuticle is open. Promise the honest walkthrough: what happens in the chair step by step, realistic before-and-after expectations by brow type (sparse vs unruly vs fair-haired), longevity of each half (lamination 4-6 weeks, tint 2-4, so the combo re-books on the tint), quick aftercare rules, and typical combo pricing. Then the flip for brow techs: the combo lifts average ticket, the mismatched fade cycle IS the rebooking hook, and before-and-after photos are the highest-converting content a brow tech can put on a booking site. No em-dashes.

sections.title: What lamination plus tint actually does
sections.direction: Shape vs color explained plainly. Why the order matters (tint after lamination, open cuticle absorbs deeper). What a session looks like start to finish, roughly 45-60 minutes.

sections.title: Realistic before and after, by brow type
sections.direction: This section targets the 6600/mo before-and-after keyword. Describe transformations honestly by starting point: sparse, unruly, fair-haired, over-plucked. What the combo cannot do (it does not add hair). Encourage viewing a tech's real before-and-after gallery before booking.

sections.title: How long it lasts and the aftercare that protects it
sections.direction: Lamination 4-6 weeks, tint 2-4; the combo re-books on the faster-fading half. First-24-hours rules (dry brows, no makeup on them), then low-maintenance. Keep aftercare tight; the dedicated aftercare SERP is franchise-owned and off-intent.

sections.title: Selling the combo and the photos that book it
sections.direction: Bundle pricing vs a la carte, the 4-week rebooking prompt, and before-and-after photos as the conversion engine: BKRDY sites have a built-in Before and After section brow techs can fill from their phone. Internal: /blog/brow-lamination-cost/, /for-estheticians/, /guides/how-much-deposit-to-charge/.

research.serpNotes: Supplier brands (PLA Pro, Beautiful Brows, Supercilium, Lash Lift Store), one franchise blog (Lash Lounge), local studios and spas. No SaaS, no editorial authority, explainer format. STRONG-to-MODERATE opening; validated 2026-07-19.
